_comment: bb-auth access file (JSON) — the REAL access gate (Cognito self-signup is open).
Re-checked on every /auth/validate, so an edit + `systemctl reload bb-auth` (SIGHUP)
takes effect on the next request; a plain restart works too. Emails match
case-insensitively. Three sibling sections, three different questions:
sites   — URL areas and the properties that hold for them. A site describes a
PLACE, never a person: no field of it may name a user.
denied  — a veto by email. Outranks every grant, on every credential.
users   — the roster: who is enrolled, what they may reach, and their API keys.
GRANTS. A request is authorized when the credential resolves to an identity and one
of exactly two sources covers the request URL: the user's `authorized_urls`, or a
site with `public_auth: true`. ACCESS IS ENUMERATED, NEVER ASSUMED — a user with no
authorized_urls (or an empty list) reaches nothing, and a URL with no site is not
open. To grant everything, say so: ['*://*/*'].
SITES. `public_auth: true` opens a URL area to ANY identity Cognito vouches for,
enrolled or not — that is the point: it is how someone who has just registered
reaches an onboarding area. Since Cognito self-signup is open, this means anyone who
can register. The app still gets X-Auth-Email and can enroll them. `public_auth`
does not help an API key: an unknown bbk_ key is nobody, not a new user.
`login_url` (absolute https) overrides BB_AUTH_LOGIN_URL for this area: on a 401 the
gate names it in X-Auth-Login-URL and nginx redirects there (see README).
FIRST MATCH WINS, in file order: the first site whose urls cover the request answers
for it — for public_auth AND for login_url — even if it grants nothing. Put specific
sites before broad ones.
A site only ever GRANTS; the only thing that takes access away is `denied`.
Unknown fields inside a site are a hard error (a typo in a future restriction must
not fail open), so no `notes` in there — unlike users and keys, which ignore extras.
There is NO per-site logout landing page: a logout happens at /auth/logout, which no
site's urls cover, so there is nothing to resolve. The logout link says where to go:
Sign out (rd is open-redirect guarded)
DENIED. Not the same as deleting the user's row. On a public_auth site the roster is
never consulted, so for an un-enrolled identity this is the ONLY denial there is. And
for an enrolled one it is a suspension, not a deletion: scope and keys survive the
lockout, so re-enabling is one edit. NOTE it cannot revoke an id_token or a cookie
mid-flight — those are stateless — but the very next /auth/validate denies.
KEYS are addressed by `key_hash` = SHA-256 of the bbk_ bearer (mint with
bb-auth-adm key add); the raw key is never stored here. `duration`: <n>d / <n>h / 0 /
never, counted from `released`. A key without authorized_urls inherits its user's.
WILDCARDS, valid in every URL component: `*` = any run of characters but never `/` —
EXCEPT as the final character, where it swallows the rest of the URL, slashes
included; `&` = exactly one character, never `/`. So `/app1/*` covers the whole /app1
subtree while `/app1*` would also match /app1-admin — always put the `/` before the
`*`. And `/app1/*` does NOT match a bare `/app1`: list both, as below.
Validate a file before deploying it: `bb-auth --check-users FILE`.

users.notes: browser login, confined to the app host
listed but reaches nothing — an empty list is a deliberate lockout. NOTE it does NOT keep them off a public_auth site; that is what `denied` is for.

api_keys.notes: example only — mint a real one with: bb-auth-adm key add bot@example.com --id laptop
